headline: One-off charges sink earnings while core utility grows
summary_short: Eversource's Q2 2026 GAAP EPS fell to $0.14 from $0.96 a year ago as a $0.30/share Aquarion divestiture charge and a $0.43/share offshore-wind liability charge overwhelmed underlying growth; non-GAAP recurring EPS was $0.87 and the company reaffirmed 2026 non-GAAP EPS guidance of $4.57-$4.72.
summary_long: GAAP EPS of $0.14 (down from $0.96 y/y) reflects two one-off items: a $0.30/share after-tax charge on the completed sale of Aquarion Water (closed June 30, 2026) and a $0.43/share charge from a higher offshore-wind contingent liability tied to the 2024 sale of South Fork and Revolution Wind. Non-GAAP recurring EPS was $0.87. Electric distribution earnings rose to $170.4M (from $161.5M) on Massachusetts/New Hampshire base-rate increases; transmission earnings fell to $183.7M (from $208.0M) on a FERC-ordered ROE cut to 9.57% and higher interest expense. Total cash rose sharply q/q to $1,819.3M. Eversource reaffirmed full-year 2026 non-GAAP EPS guidance of $4.57-$4.72 and its 5-7% long-term EPS growth rate through 2030.
